shorts.title: What you will learn: Memory and addresses
shorts.hook: Every variable has a home address.
shorts.script: Every variable has a home address. Today we look under the hood. Every variable lives at an address in memory. Soon you will use that address. Memory is a long row of bytes. Each byte has a number, called its address. A variable lives at one address, and it fills as many bytes as its type needs. The ampersand in front of a variable gives its address. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: What you will learn: Memory and addresses.

shorts.title: Memory and addresses in one minute
shorts.hook: Memory is a long row of bytes.
shorts.script: Memory is a long row of bytes. Each byte has a number, called its address. A variable lives at one address, and it fills as many bytes as its type needs. The ampersand in front of a variable gives its address. Think of a street of houses. Each house has a number, and a family lives inside. An array of three ints. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Memory and addresses in one minute.

shorts.title: Inside the second program
shorts.script: A char takes one byte. An int takes four. A double takes eight. An address itself takes eight bytes on a sixty-four-bit computer. Remember this. We will store addresses in variables soon. The program prints one, four, eight and eight on four lines. Memory is a long row of numbered bytes. Every variable lives at an address. The ampersand gives the address of a variable. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Inside the second program.

shorts.title: Bug of the Day: Storing an address in an int
shorts.hook: Can you spot the bug in memory and addresses?
shorts.script: Can you spot the bug in memory and addresses? Bug of the Day. We store the address of fish in a plain int. The compiler says invalid conversion from int star to int. An address has its own type. For the address of an int, that type is int star. We learn it in the next episode. An address has its own type. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Bug of the Day: Storing an address in an int.

shorts.title: Pun and challenge
shorts.hook: Can you find the gap between two doubles in memory and addresses?
shorts.script: Can you find the gap between two doubles in memory and addresses? My variable moved house. It left a new address, but it forgot to tell its neighbours. Make an array of two doubles. Print the number of bytes between the two items. Write your answer in the comments. Memory is a long row of numbered bytes. Every variable lives at an address. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Pun and challenge.
